previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 65-year-old man with a history of CNS B-cell lymphoma in remission was admitted for scheduled high-dose methotrexate chemotherapy. He tolerated the infusion well, with methotrexate levels declining appropriately to 0.13 by discharge. He reported ongoing episodes of left facial numbness and dysarthria, concerning for partial seizures or possible disease recurrence. A bedside EEG showed no seizure activity on preliminary review, and a lamotrigine level was sent but remained pending at discharge. The patient declined an in-hospital brain MRI due to prior commitments but agreed to outpatient imaging the following week. His diabetes insipidus and hypertension were managed without complication, and he was discharged home with a plan to complete a short course of leucovorin and sodium bicarbonate, continue his regular medications including temozolomide, and follow up in clinic with MRI and neurology evaluation. The next chemotherapy cycle is anticipated in six months pending outpatient findings.
problems: Unspecified B-cell lymphoma, extranodal and solid organ sites
Localization-related (focal) (partial) symptomatic epilepsy and epileptic syndromes with simple partial seizures, not intractable, without status epilepticus
